q6.answer: Events on the broker drive each step: each service consumes an event, saves its change and the next event in one transaction (outbox), and a relay publishes it. There is no central orchestrator. The record of progress is the Order service's status field on the order (PLACED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID_CLAIMING, CONFIRMED or a CANCELLED status), which the customer polls via GET /orders/{id}.

q7.answer: The provider calls a webhook on Payment, which verifies the signature, finds the payment by order id and saves the outcome. Payment then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker (via its outbox), and Order consumes it and moves the order on.

q8.answer: Two layers. At the webhook, Payment stores the provider's event id in a unique table of processed events, in the same transaction as the payment status change, and replies 200 OK without doing anything for a repeat. Between services, every consumer records handled event ids and drops redelivered ones. Order also acts on each event only in the status it expects.

q9.answer: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, Order sets CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled, and Inventory consumes that and releases the reservation if it is still HELD, so the stock goes back on sale. If the hold is already EXPIRED, RELEASED or missing, Inventory does nothing. The expiry timer also returns it after 10 minutes in any case.

q10.answer: Order checks that it is still AWAITING_PAYMENT, then sends ClaimStock, and Inventory decides inside one transaction. If the hold is still HELD it claims it. If it is EXPIRED it tries once to take all lines again, and if every line is available it claims them and the order is fulfilled. If any line is short, or the reservation is RELEASED or missing, it publishes StockClaimFailed and Order cancels as out of stock and requests a full refund. The re-take is an assumption of this design that can be removed.

q11.answer: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING in Payment's database (saved before the provider call, with an attempt count). A retry timer re-sends it with backoff and never gives up, using the refund's own idempotency key so it cannot refund twice. After 5 failures it also alerts operations. It leaves pending only by succeeding, which publishes RefundSucceeded.

q12.answer: Order setting CONFIRMED and publishing OrderConfirmed causes it. The Cart service consumes OrderConfirmed from the broker and empties the cart, only if the order id in the event matches the order id it saved on the cart. Otherwise it ignores the event.
